findings.reason: the ship-on/off decision is the node's whole deliverable; without a repeat or a stated margin it can be taken on a coin flip, sending the rerank into the product or leaving it out for a reason that is not the one the section asserts.
findings.text: §7's done-when decides "the switch ships on only if the role-aware rerank beats fusion alone on both mean nDCG@10 and grade-3 precision@5" from one scoring pass, while §7 says at line 307 that "its order varies between runs" and the harness scores each arm once (tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py:340 `score_arm` loops the questions once, no repeat), so a margin of the size §1 reports (rerank nDCG 0.695–0.697 vs fusion 0.686) can fall either way on run noise — the gate can pass or fail on variance rather than on the rerank earning its place.

findings.reason: the two deliverables close on different verdicts — the product change on whether it is correct and installed, the measurement on whether it is trusted — so a node that carries both cannot be closed on one, and a worker must decide which half a blocked verdict applies to.
findings.text: §7 says "the second scores the arms and decides the switch", but that same node also lands shipped product code that §7's first paragraph adds (the signal state builder at line 293, the role-aware question "moved into the product beside `_RERANK_QUESTION`" at line 313, and the `_search_signals` rerank routing at line 292), so one node carries both a product change reviewable in its own right and a measurement whose outcome may be "ships off" with no product change at all.
